primitives.name: Angular Defensive Pressure
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our contributions include (i) a novel "angular pressure" metric, (ii) logic for pre-shot pass sequences, and (iii) an open pipeline and app for xG analysis.
primitives.assumptions: Defenders' positions are modeled as angular contributions inversely weighted by squared distance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When defender positions collapse into a single line, angular pressure becomes undefined.

primitives.name: Pre-Shot Pass Sequence
primitives.verbatim_quote: Using StatsBomb event data, we implement thorough cleaning (merging event and lineup JSON, extracting freeze-frame defense data) and engineer novel features (angular defensive pressure, goalkeeper distance, pre-shot sequence).
primitives.assumptions: Pass events are tracked within a fixed temporal window of 5 events before the shot.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When fewer than 5 events exist, sequence length is truncated.

layer2.telemetry: Correlation with shot quality via permutation importance.

reasoning_traces.think:
The framework integrates geometric and contextual features into a unified probabilistic shot quality model. Angular pressure is derived from defender positions, capturing spatial density around the shooter. Pre-shot pass sequences encode tactical buildup complexity, influencing shot selection. Game state context adjusts shot quality based on scoreline and match progression. These primitives are combined in an XGBoost model with calibrated outputs. The model's strength lies in its ability to disentangle static shot features (distance, angle) from dynamic context (defensive geometry, game state). Failure modes arise when defensive positioning collapses or when game state is misinterpreted due to lack of temporal resolution. Multicollinearity between distance and goalkeeper distance necessitates variance inflation factor checks. The SHAP analysis confirms that these features contribute meaningfully to model discrimination and calibration.
